issues.description: The solution implementation declares the Lecture attributes using snake_case names (e.g., 'lecture_name', 'number_of_inscribed_students') but the constructor, getters, setters, and other methods use camelCase field names (e.g., 'lectureName', 'numberOfInscribedStudents'). This naming mismatch inside the solution causes a structural inconsistency that will lead to compilation errors and also deviates from the UML and problem description which use camelCase attribute names.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the attribute declarations with the rest of the code and the UML by using the camelCase field names shown in the specification (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). Concretely, rename the snake_case fields in the solution to the camelCase names, or update all uses to match the declared names, ensuring the template, solution, and UML all use the same attribute identifiers.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify attributes using camelCase names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). The solution implementation declares the fields using snake_case (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) but the constructor, getters and setters use camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, ...). This mismatch creates a conceptual mapping barrier for students (they expect camelCase attributes from the UML) and also results in inconsistent identifiers inside the solution code (likely a compile/runtime confusion).
issues.suggestedFix: Use consistent camelCase attribute names throughout to match the UML and problem statement. Rename the fields in the solution to: private String lectureName; private int numberOfInscribedStudents; private int numberOfGuestStudents; private int numberOfLecturers; private int numberOfTutors; and ensure the constructor, getters, setters and other methods refer to these same camelCase fields.
